biggestGap: celestial-large is a naked featureless mannequin: blank egg head with two flat white dot eyes, no mouth, no nose, no hair, no garment, no radiance, and six flat opaque paddle blades on one side standing in for wings. Give the archetype an actual designed body — a mass event at the shoulder, a real face zone (brow shadow, recessed sockets, a mouth or maw), and layered feather groups (primaries/secondaries/coverts as separate silhouette forms) split left and right — before any other fix.
notes:
DRAGON (idle) — reference wins. The neck is a constant-diameter tube that plugs into the torso with a hard step and no shoulder merge, and the fore and hind limbs are the same stubby column so there is no haunch mass anywhere in the silhouette; the black-drake ref tapers its neck into a shoulder and loads visible weight into the hindquarters. The head sculpt is genuinely good — brow ridges, slit pupils, horn sweep, faceted skull planes — and holds its own against the ref head.

DRAGON-WALK (spread wing) — reference wins, decisively. The membrane is NOT one unbroken sheet from body to wingtip: a bare cylindrical humerus runs from the shoulder knob up to the elbow knuckle with open sky on both sides of it, and the membrane only begins above that elbow, so the wing reads as a flag on a pole with the brachiopatagium missing entirely. Every trailing edge is a dead-straight line with zero sag or scallop between fingers, and the far wing shows bare strut spokes crossing open sky where the sheet should be filled — the drake ref closes the shoulder-to-elbow gap and scallops every finger bay.

SERPENT (three-headed by design) — reference wins. The face close-up is the strongest single asset on the wall: fang rows, a dark maw, faceted skull plates, real menace. But the body lies flat on the grass as a bent noodle with no S-curve lift, and the two flanking heads are nubs pressed against the main neck with no necks of their own, so the three-head design does not read; the Valheim serpent rears in a tall S with a spiked crest and mottled scale value breaks while ours is one flat green value from head to tail tip.

OOZE — no ooze reference exists in the library, so judged against shipped-game slimes (Slime Rancher, Dragon Quest, Minecraft, Diablo gelatinous mobs). Reference wins. The translucent shell over a darker inner core is a real material read and the pseudopod skirt gives it a contact edge, but the whole mass is one flat teal value with no specular hot spot, no debris or bone suspended inside, and no face — the close-up panel is a blank wall of teal with a single stray orange dot; shipped slimes always carry a rim/spec hit and something visible in the goo.

BEAST-LARGE — reference wins, badly. A uniform-diameter grey tube runs from shoulder to hip with no ribcage, no shoulder hump and no haunch swell, all four limbs are the same width root to toe, and the neck is a straight pipe with a lumpy head stuck on the end. The Valheim boar and WoW worg both put a large mass event at the shoulder, taper the waist, differentiate fore from hind, and break the silhouette with bristle or fur; this is exactly the sausage-lizard read the campaign named.

CELESTIAL-LARGE — reference wins, worst of the seven. A naked featureless tan mannequin: blank egg head, two flat white dot eyes, no mouth, no nose, no hair, no garment, and nothing celestial — no halo, no light, no radiance. The wings are a bank of six flat opaque paddle blades stacked on one side that read as a folding fan rather than feathers; even the Greydwarf Brute, a low-tier trash mob, carries ruffed shoulders, gnarled forearms and a face.

ELEMENTAL-LARGE — reference wins, but this is the closest subject on the wall and the round's real progress. It now genuinely reads as an earth golem: overlapping stone mass, oversized dark claw hands as the biggest limbs, planted taloned feet, moss lumps on the crown, a sunken face zone with two glowing eyes in a dark recessed socket band, heavy ink weight. The gap is that every plate is a ROUNDED COBBLE, so the silhouette is all convex bubbles — a stack of grey potatoes — where the earth-golem refs use large angular slabs with straight fracture edges and deep dark recessed joints; and there is no crack glow anywhere in the body, leaving the whole mass one flat mid-grey with only arbitrary brown patches that read as mud stains rather than as separate stone.

HARNESS: no broken panels. The hard-edged sky band in the close-up panels is the known finite ground-disc rim, not a bug.
